decisions.reason: Introduces Causal-LoCoMo, 'a causally annotated benchmark derived from long conversational data, where each example contains a user request, a structured memory bank, useful memories, irrelevant distractors, and synthetic harmful memories', and evaluates against 'vector, graph, reflection, summary, full-history, and no-memory baselines' -- a benchmark/methodology characterising agent memory selection, which T6 keeps in scope.

MemPro's Evolving Agent 'iteratively selects promising versions, diagnoses recurring failures, and creates improved child versions' of the memory construction-retrieval pipeline itself, i.e. the agent writes and revises its own memory system at run time -- T2 keeps it in.

The contribution is enlarging attendable past context ('LongMem can thus memorize long past context... typically enlarge the long-form memory to 65k tokens... to benefit various downstream tasks' via in-context learning), which T4 treats as more room rather than a policy over what persists; the abstract never frames this as an interactive agent, only a language-modeling backbone, so no cross-turn agent state is described (E6).

Compares only two static substrates -- 'per-user gamma-LoRA (a small LoRA adapter trained on each user's history)', a parametric mechanism with no run-time externalised store (E2), against 'BGE-large dense top-K retrieval', a fixed-corpus classical RAG comparator (E3). No mechanism where an agent itself writes memory at run time is described.

Hard call: 'The memory stores facts and rules in both natural language and symbolic forms, enabling precise tracking' and the framework 'iteratively performs symbolic rule grounding and LLM-based rule implementation', i.e. the system writes to and reads back from its own memory across the iterative reasoning steps. The abstract does not say whether this persistence extends beyond a single query, so per the uncertainty rule for T2 it is kept in rather than guessed out.

Mela integrates the Hierarchical Memory Module into a Transformer decoder to 'perform online memory consolidation at test time' so that it 'maintains performance on significantly longer contexts, whereas Transformer baselines degrade rapidly' -- an architecture-level context-extension contribution (T4->E1), evaluated purely as a language model with no agent, turns or sessions described (E6).

MemSkill's controller and 'LLM-based executor' produce 'skill-guided memories' from interaction traces, and a designer 'evolves the skill set by proposing refinements' after reviewing hard cases -- the agent itself extracts, consolidates and prunes its memory at run time, squarely satisfying T2.

The only memory-adjacent content is verifying 'the model retains its general capabilities without significant catastrophic forgetting after training' following knowledge distillation and fine-tuning -- a parametric, weights-only effect with no externalised store an agent reads or writes, and no agent or cross-turn behaviour is described at all.

MementoCore 'modularizes memory control into specialized operators for step processing, memory compression, episodic writing, and episodic selection', with 'working memory selectively preserves task-relevant interface events' and 'episodic memory retrieves reusable past trajectories' -- the GUI agent explicitly writes and later retrieves its own memory across a long-horizon task.

Echo's episodic-memory capability is instilled by training: 'Temporal information is innovatively incorporated into the LLM training process, and Echo is trained using the EM-Train' -- this is a parametric fine-tuning approach baking episodic recall into weights, with no externalised store the deployed agent writes to or reads from at run time.
